```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

H1: People with lower perceived social class will have more collectivist attitudes. 

H2: People who value gender equality will report higher overall romantic love with their partner.

## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
rm(list = ls())
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("data/raw/data_doctored.csv")

#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows
dim(raw)
head(raw[,c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth")])
str(raw)

#make data with ID, gender equality, collectivism/individualism values, and love values; keep raw unchanged

data <- raw[,c("ResponseId","cot_class",
               "Individualism_col_1", "Individualism_col_2",
               "Individualism_col_3", "Individualism_col_4",
               "Gender_Equality_1",
               "Gender_Equality_2", "Gender_Equality_3",
               "Love_1", "Love_2", "Love_3", "Love_4",
               "Love_5", "Love_6", "Love_7", "Love_8",
               "Love_9", "Love_10", "Love_11", "Love_12",
               "Love_13", "Love_14", "Love_15")]
dim(data)
str(data)

```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participant_ids}

#count na - there is 1 NA for response ID, and 17093 for gender equality
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))
sum(is.na(data$Gender_Equality_1))

#count blank - there are zero
sum(data$ResponseId=="", na.rm = TRUE)

#count duplicates - 0 duplicates!
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#can get a nice big summary description block!
summary(data$ResponseId)

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID,]) # whole row is NAs so fine to delete

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count - should be 1 less
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

```


## 3. Clean perceived social class 

```{r social class record }
# codebook: cot_class, 1=Lower; 2=Lower middle; 3=Middle; 4=Upper middle; 5=Upper.
table(data$cot_class, useNA = "ifany") # look at data spread, a lot of NA

#turn cot_class into a factor with labels Lower, Lower middle, Middle, Upper Middle, and Upper

data$cot_class <- factor(data$cot_class,
                         c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
                         c("Lower", "Lower middle", "Middle", 
                           "Upper Middle", "Upper"))

```


## 4. Validate collectivism values, calculate mean and make H1 dataset

```{r validate collective behavior}
###JK: Please recode the missing-value markers before converting these items to numbers. ###
# as.numeric() does not turn -99 into NA: -99 is already a number.
# "N/A" and blank text can become NA with a warning, but it is clearer to explicitly handle all the missing codes listed in the codebook first.
# Your H1 uses items 1, 2, and 4. Here is a replacement for the four as.numeric() lines immediately below. Use this before calculating scores.
# collect_items <- c("Individualism_col_1", "Individualism_col_2",
#                    "Individualism_col_4")
# for (i in collect_items) {
#   data[data[, i] %in% c("-99", "N/A", "NA", ""), i] <- NA
#   data[, i] <- as.numeric(data[, i])
# }
###  End of comment ###

#group all 4 individualism/collectivism variables and make them numeric
data$Individualism_col_1 <- as.numeric(data$Individualism_col_1)
data$Individualism_col_2 <- as.numeric(data$Individualism_col_2)
data$Individualism_col_3 <- as.numeric(data$Individualism_col_3)
data$Individualism_col_4 <- as.numeric(data$Individualism_col_4)


collect <- c("Individualism_col_1", "Individualism_col_2",
               "Individualism_col_3", "Individualism_col_4")

#see summary of variables
summary(data[,collect])

#count NAs
colSums(is.na(data[,collect]))

###JK: These are separate 1-7 ratings, not a fixed-total allocation task. ###
# For example, answering 4 on each of four items gives a total of 16, which is perfectly valid. The responses do not need to add up to 28.
# Each item should be between 1 and 7, not between 0 and 28.
# Replace the total-score and range checks below (through collect_range) with checks on the three items you actually use in your score:
# summary(data[, collect_items])
# colSums(is.na(data[, collect_items]))
# colSums(data[, collect_items] < 1 | data[, collect_items] > 7, na.rm = TRUE)
# If the last line reports any values outside 1-7, inspect them before scoring.
###  End of comment ###

#calculate total score; leave the total NA if any item is missing
data$collect_total <- rowSums(data[,collect], na.rm = FALSE)
summary(data$collect)

#count those that do not sum to 28
sum(data$collect_total != 28 & !is.na(data$collect_total))

#check that each observed allocation is between 0 and 28
data$collect_range <- rowSums(
  data[, collect] < 0 | data[,collect] > 28,
  na.rm = TRUE
) == FALSE

#make h1Data with ID, socioeconomic class, and cleaned collectivism variables, and avg value for overall collectivism (avg of q1,2,4)

###JK: Please create h1_data before referring to it in a calculation. ###
# The assignment h1_data <- ... happens only after the right-hand side finishes.
# In the code below, mutate() and select() refer to h1_data before it exists.
# In a fresh R session, this stops with "object 'h1_data' not found".
# Also, your positive-value checks cover items 2, 3, and 4, but not item 1.
# Item 3 does not contribute to your mean, so requiring an answer to it unnecessarily excludes people who answered all three items you need.
# After the missing-value cleaning suggested above, replace the pipeline below (from h1_data <- through mutate()) with these separate steps:
# h1_data <- data[, c("ResponseId", "cot_class", collect_items)]
# h1_data <- h1_data[complete.cases(h1_data), ]
# h1_data$collect_avg <- rowMeans(h1_data[, collect_items], na.rm = FALSE)
###  End of comment ###

h1_data <- data %>%
  select("ResponseId", "cot_class", "Individualism_col_1", "Individualism_col_2",
               "Individualism_col_3", "Individualism_col_4") %>%
  filter(!is.na(data$Individualism_col_1) & !is.na(data$Individualism_col_2) &
        !is.na(data$Individualism_col_3) & !is.na(data$Individualism_col_4) &
         data$Individualism_col_2 > 0 & data$Individualism_col_3 > 0 &
          data$Individualism_col_4 > 0) %>%
  mutate(h1_data, collect_avg = rowMeans(select(h1_data,
                                              c("Individualism_col_1",
                                                "Individualism_col_2",
                                                "Individualism_col_4")),
                                         na.rm = TRUE))
 
#checking if -99 is gone, it wasn't so filtered those out
summary(h1_data)

#some basic subtraction, total number of NAs was 19,555 and original number of observations was 117,293 so that would leave us with 97738 observations left, but then 6 got filtered out because they were -99, leaving us with the final number in h1_data being 97732
#117293 - 97732 = 19561 (19555 NAs + 6 -99 )

###JK: na.omit() already acts on the table passed through the pipe. ###
# The extra H1data$cot_class argument is unnecessary, and H1data also has different capitalization from H1Data. To keep this step straightforward:
# H1Data <- h1_data %>%
#   select(ResponseId, cot_class, collect_avg) %>%
#   na.omit()
###  End of comment ###

H1Data <- h1_data %>%
  select("ResponseId", "cot_class", "collect_avg") %>%
  na.omit(H1data$cot_class)

```


## 5. Validate equality and love data
```{r make clean h2 dataset subset}
#load data
h2_data_raw <- data %>%
  select("ResponseId", "Gender_Equality_1",
         "Gender_Equality_2", "Gender_Equality_3",
         "Love_1", "Love_2", "Love_3", "Love_4",
         "Love_5", "Love_6", "Love_7", "Love_8",
         "Love_9", "Love_10", "Love_11", "Love_12",
         "Love_13", "Love_14", "Love_15")


# check for NAs, there are a lot, pick highest value and filter that one
#still a few -99 and empty spots, filter these p
summary(h2_data_raw)


###JK: Clean all three gender-equality items before filtering or reversing them. ###
# na.omit() removes actual NA values, but not the text "N/A", blanks, or -99.
# The filter below checks only items 1 and 3, leaving item 2 unchecked.
# It also compares values with 0 before converting the columns to numeric.
# Your saved H2 scores match the raw data, but these checks do not reliably handle every missing-value marker documented for all three items.
# Replace the block below, from h2_data_1 <- through the three as.numeric() lines, with this code. Then keep your existing 8 - x reversal code.

# equality_items <- paste0("Gender_Equality_", 1:3)
# for (item in equality_items) {
#   h2_data_raw[h2_data_raw[, item] %in% c("-99", "N/A", "NA", ""), item] <- NA
#   h2_data_raw[, item] <- as.numeric(h2_data_raw[, item])
# }
# summary(h2_data_raw[, equality_items])
# colSums(h2_data_raw[, equality_items] < 1 |
#         h2_data_raw[, equality_items] > 7, na.rm = TRUE)
# love_items <- paste0("Love_", 1:15)
# colSums(h2_data_raw[, love_items] < 1 |
#         h2_data_raw[, love_items] > 5, na.rm = TRUE)

# If these range checks find unexpected values, inspect them before continuing.

# H2_data_cln <- na.omit(h2_data_raw)

# This keeps your current rule: require all 3 equality and all 15 love items.
# The special missing code here is -99, not 999; please update that comment too.
###  End of comment ###

#clean dataset with filtered NAs and 0s and 999s, checked NAs with summary
h2_data_1 <- na.omit(h2_data_raw)

#clear out 999s
H2_data_cln <- h2_data_1 %>%
  filter(h2_data_1$Gender_Equality_1 > 0 & h2_data_1$Gender_Equality_3 > 0)

#make variables numeric 
H2_data_cln$Gender_Equality_1 <- as.numeric(H2_data_cln$Gender_Equality_1)
H2_data_cln$Gender_Equality_2 <- as.numeric(H2_data_cln$Gender_Equality_2)
H2_data_cln$Gender_Equality_3 <- as.numeric(H2_data_cln$Gender_Equality_3)

#reverse code values
h2_data_rev <- H2_data_cln %>%
  mutate(across("Gender_Equality_1":"Gender_Equality_3", ~ 8 - .)) %>%
  rename("Gender_Equality_1R" = "Gender_Equality_1", "Gender_Equality_2R" = "Gender_Equality_2", "Gender_Equality_3R" = "Gender_Equality_3" )

is.numeric(H2_data_cln$Gender_Equality_3)
```

## 6. Create mean variables for H2 
```{r mean variables for H2}
#likert scales
#gender equal: 1-7, higher means more value of gender roles, so reverse code shows value of gender equality
#overall love: 1-5, higher means more overall romantic love

#h2 avgs, means of both gender equality and love questions
h2_data_avgs <- h2_data_rev %>%
  mutate(h2_data_rev, 
         love_avg = rowMeans(select(h2_data_rev,
                                              c("Love_1":"Love_15")),
                                         na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(h2_data_rev, 
         gen_eq_avg = rowMeans(select(h2_data_rev,
                                              c("Gender_Equality_1R":"Gender_Equality_3R")),
                                         na.rm = TRUE))

#just final values!
H2Data <- h2_data_avgs %>%
  select("ResponseId", "love_avg", "gen_eq_avg")
```


## 7. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(H1Data)
str(H1Data)
head(H1Data)
colSums(is.na(H1Data))
table(H1Data$cot_class,useNA="ifany")
range(H1Data$collect_avg)
sum(duplicated(H1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; both scores should be within 1-7
dim(H2Data)
str(H2Data)
head(H2Data)
colSums(is.na(H2Data))
range(H2Data$love_avg)
range(H2Data$gen_eq_avg)
sum(duplicated(H2Data$ResponseId))

#all of it checks out! yay!
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units

###JK: Please correct the collectivism scale description: it is 1-7, not 1-5. ###
# Its anchors are "Definitely disagree" and "Definitely agree".
# You can replace the H1 label assignment below with:
# var_label(H1Data) <- c(
#   "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
#   "Self-reported social class: 1=Lower, 2=Lower middle, 3=Middle, 4=Upper middle, 5=Upper; stored as labeled categories.",
#   "Collectivism: mean of Individualism_col_1, 2, and 4; all three responses required. Items are 1=Definitely disagree to 7=Definitely agree. No reversal; higher scores indicate greater collectivism."
# )
###  End of comment ###

var_label(H1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Reported socal class: original codes 1=Lower, 2=Lower middle, 3=Middle,
  4=Upper Middle, 5=Upper; now stored as a factor 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)",
  "Average reported collectivist values: Average score across 3 questions on a Likert scale from 1-5, 1 = Strongly disagree, 5 = Strongly agree, zero is not valid"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule

###JK: These labels are assigned by column position, so the two score labels are swapped. ###
# H2Data is ordered ResponseId, love_avg, gen_eq_avg, but the descriptions below put gender equality before love. Also, Love items are 1-5, not 1-7.
# Replace the H2 label assignment below with:
# var_label(H2Data) <- c(
#   "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
#   "Overall romantic love: mean of Love_1-15; all 15 responses required. Items are 1=Not at all to 5=Extremely. No reversal; higher scores indicate greater romantic love.",
#   "Gender equality: mean of Gender_Equality_1-3 after reversing each item with 8 - x; all three responses required. Scores range from 1 to 7; higher scores indicate greater endorsement of gender equality."
# )
# Please also update the earlier final-table comment: love_avg should be within 1-5, while gen_eq_avg should be within 1-7.
###  End of comment ###

var_label(H2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Average belief in gender equality: average of 3 reverse-coded questions,
   1 = Definitely disagree, 7= Definitely agree, after reverse-code, higher scores are associated with more belief in gender equality, zero is not valid",
  "Overall romantic love: mean of 15 questions, each 1 = Not at all to 7 = Extremely; no reverse coding, zero is not valid"
)

```

H1 includes participants with an ID, valid reported perceived social class, and a valid average collectivisism score based on valid responses to 3 related questions. Factor level numbers in the generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(H1Data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, average gender equality belief score based on 3 valid responses to gender equality questions and average overall romantic love score based on 15 valid responses to love questions.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(H2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(H1Data,"data/processed_data/LRpractice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(H2Data,"data/processed_data/LRpractice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
H1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/LRpractice_h1.csv")
H2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/LRpractice_h2.csv")
dim(H1Saved)
dim(H2Saved)

```
